title: Asymmetric rate-window aggregation causing staggered customer billing
creator: Marisa Kline
description: Several enterprise customers reported staggered and outsized invoices for the same time periods after regional failovers and traffic shifts between Hosted and Private deployments. Initial triage points to aggregation windows used in the rate-limiter/usage-rollup pipeline: different services (edge rate limiter, aggregator, and billing-rollup job) use non-aligned window boundaries (1s/10s/60s) which produces asymmetric attribution when requests cross boundaries or are replayed after transient failures. This ticket owns the investigation, short-term fix, and a safer roll-forward plan to avoid further customer billing discrepancies.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure two clients sending bursty traffic (avg 200rps) with short idle periods that cause window boundary crossing. 2) Route traffic intermittently across Hosted region A and a Private deployment via smart-routing policy. 3) Simulate a transient 2s failure at the edge causing request retries. 4) Run daily rollup job and compare per-customer per-route token counts vs live stream aggregator counts. Expect delta where requests that straddle windows are double-attributed or time-shifted into next billing bucket.
investigation_notes: 03-09: On-call received 3 escalations from enterprise customers (finance teams). Initial logs show billing spikes aligned to 00:00:10-00:00:20 UTC window boundaries.
03-09: Correlated with edge retry logs — many retries carry same client-id + request-id but different trace ids when crossing region during failover.
03-10: Rolled debug build with added correlation id forwarding; observed aggregator receives both original and retry events due to request replay from smart-routing after failover.

03-11: Found that edge rate-limiter tags events with window_start at 1s alignment, aggregator groups into 10s buckets, billing-rollup summarizes into 60s buckets; reconciliation pipeline assumes idempotent dedupe only within same bucket, not across different bucket granularities.
03-12: Discovered a race where KV-cache eviction on Private nodes causes requests to be reissued to Hosted with new request id; no cross-system dedupe key present.
03-12: Customer-impact assessment: 4 customers affected, overcharge amount ranges from 2% to 18% for the impacted invoice period; high SLA risk for enterprise accounts.
03-13: Added synthetic tests and telemetry to run on staging that simulate boundary-crossing bursts; confirmed deltas reproducible.
03-13: Drafted short-term mitigation and long-term design in proposed_fixes.
03-13: Notified finance and account teams; issuing manual adjustments for affected invoices pending fix deployment.
proposed_fixes: Short-term (hotfix): Align rollup windows across rate-limiter, aggregator, and billing-rollup: change aggregator to use 1s boundaries and make billing-rollup slide-aligned to 1s for the next billing run. Roll out to Hosted, then Private (canary 5% traffic).
Short-term (dedupe): Add cross-system idempotency key forwarding header (x-rw-cid) from edge through routing layer so retries carry a stable dedupe key for at least 120s.
Medium-term: Implement global dedupe storage in the centralized aggregator with 5min TTL and canonical request fingerprint (client_id + request_hash) to dedupe retries across bucket boundaries.

Long-term: Replace fixed-window aggregation with hybrid sliding-window counters + per-request canonicalization to ensure accurate attribution for bursty/replayed requests and improve reconciliation guarantees.
Operational: Add end-to-end reconciliation job that compares stream aggregator counts vs batch rollup and emits alerts when per-customer delta >0.5% for two consecutive windows.
Customer comms: Prepare templated credits and root-cause explanation for affected customers; coordinate with billing to auto-apply refunds where appropriate.
deploy_plan: 1) Deploy aggregator hotfix to staging; run synthetic regression (10m). 2) Canary deploy aggregator hotfix to Hosted cluster (region A) at 5% traffic for 30m. 3) Apply idempotency header change at edge proxies in same canary. 4) Monitor reconciliation metric and billing-delta alert. 5) Gradually increase to 50% then 100% over 2 hours if no regressions. 6) Coordinate a separate Private deployment plan with on-prem team (requires K8s reconcile and config sync).
rollback_plan: If aggregate deltas increase or latency regressions >5%: 1) Revert aggregator to previous image and edge header change. 2) Disable canary routing. 3) Run a curated reconciliation audit and open incident call. 4) Restore manual credits for new customer complaints until stable.
customer_reports: Acct-ACME: reported +12% invoice delta for billing period ending 2026-03-01; provided request timelines and traces.
Acct-OrionHealth: reported time-shifted token counts across two invoices; CFO flagged as urgent.
Acct-NomadApps: smaller delta (~2%) but high visibility due to audit window.
impact_summary: High customer impact for a small set of enterprise customers. Risk of churn if invoices are not corrected promptly. Root cause spans telemetry alignment, request-id propagation, and dedupe assumptions in rollup logic.
resolution: In progress. Hotfix implemented in aggregator to align aggregation windows and idempotency header is in canary. Finance applied interim manual credits for affected invoices. Full dedupe storage and sliding-window plan scheduled for next cycle (estimate 2 sprints).
